observation: Human concept review caught a wrong noun shape before any code: planner locked 'primary harness' as a setup-time stamp; founder re-shaped it to a persisted team default consumed at every agent-creation path — a schema migration the plan had avoided.

Planner classified DESIGN=routine/DOC=incremental, which by the Phase-2.5 gate rule would have SKIPPED human concept review — yet the WP explicitly flagged review=Yes and the founder's answers forced a re-architecture (persist + migration) and a reclassify to DOC=significant. Classification-based skip gate undershot a materially non-trivial change.

Founder's headline behavior ('Assistant opens ready') first shipped with only a DB-state check (stub row carries harnessType) and no runtime turn-behavior test — a regression reintroducing the notice-card burst would have stayed green. Caught at code-review round 1; fixed with a real runAssistantTurn test + required sanity-break.

The assistant-ready honest test uses real runAssistantTurn (no stub) against builtin, gated requireHarness('builtin'), registered in BUILTIN_ONLY_INTEGRATION, on the locked tiny model deepseek-v4-flash; discriminator between pass/sanity-break is registered makeBuiltinPool() vs empty AdapterPool. Honest-harness discipline held.

Builder opened PR #405 during the build phase (ahead of pipeline order build->review->retro->ship), so its attestation commit (939b34cf) went stale the moment the review-fix commit f4c53227 landed — ship must re-attest. Builder should not open the PR before retro.

AV1's spec (Track AV) was registered on origin/main via PR #401 but the local primary checkout was behind, so AV1 looked non-existent until a git fetch; worktree had to be based on the origin/main SHA because guard-main.sh blocks the literal 'main' token in the worktree-add command.

The real source of the founder's post-setup notification 'burst' was the AssistantOverlay ?onboarding=true auto-open rendering missing_key/missing_harness cards — NOT the agent-health path (a zero-session agent is idle, never error, so the health guard is a genuine no-op). Only found by tracing during concept-review revision; the first plan nearly shipped a guard that changed nothing.

currentBranch() real-git unit test had to account for os.tmpdir() on macOS living inside a git worktree (/var/folders/…), which pollutes rev-parse; captured as @lore. Test-env gotcha worth reusing for any real-git temp-dir test.

Session limit hit mid review-round-2; the reviewer died before writing its verdict. Re-spawning a fresh reviewer reproduced the review cleanly because all context (plan, diff, prior findings) lives on disk — confirms the artifact-handoff contract survives mid-phase agent death.
